description: Use 5700 years in Exercises 31 and 32; change two-half-life interval to 11,400 years. Three-half-life answers become 17,100 years.

exercises.before: <exercise id="fs-id2391582" type="conceptual-questions"><problem id="fs-id2391582-revised-problem"><para id="fs-id2391582-revised-p1">Carbon-14 has a half-life of 5730 years. Assume a closed sample initially contained 8000 carbon-14 atoms and now contains about 1000. How many half-lives have passed, and what age does this suggest? Explain why this is an estimate rather than an exact clock for each atom.</para></problem></exercise>
